test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What price should a shopkeeper mark on an article, which costs him Rs. 153, to gain 20% after allowing a discount of 15%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)** is given by the ratio: **CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)**.

Ratio CP : MP = (100 − 15) : (100 + 20) = 85 : 120.

Simplify the ratio by dividing by 5: **17 : 24**.

Given CP = 17 units = **Rs. 153**. Multiplier = 153 ÷ 17 = 9.

MP = 24 units × 9 = **Rs. 216**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Cost Price (CP)** = Rs. 153, **Profit%** = 20%, **Discount%** = 15%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | MP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/797b88c7d3fd1fc4302aa9d5683bc778623d331152540c95efca707e9c90a0c9.png] 
⇒ First, calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 153 × (120 ÷ 100) = 153 × 1.2 = **Rs. 183.6**.
⇒ Now, calculate **Marked Price (MP)**: 183.6 = MP × (100 − 15) ÷ 100.
⇒ 183.6 = MP × (85 ÷ 100) ⇒ MP = (183.6 × 100) ÷ 85.
⇒ MP = 18360 ÷ 85 = **Rs. 216**.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 216.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

**Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the Marked Price to reach the Selling Price.

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the **Marked Price** is higher than the **Cost Price**. Formula: Markup% = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.</p
